statements.t: The benefit we would have otherwise expected to realize from such favorable weather conditions, however, was partially offset by lower than anticipated volumes from certain production facilities which flow exclusively through our pipeline transportation network.
We continue to focus on rightsizing and optimizing our capital structure, expecting to drive future cash savings to add to those already realized from the steps we took earlier this year.

Our capital allocation priorities remain unchanged as we expect to continue to retire our highest-cost capital, reduce our debt in absolute terms, and thoughtfully and prudently grow distributions to our common unitholders over time, while preserving our financial flexibility to pursue attractive organic and inorganic opportunities as they emerge in the future.

As noted above, however, that benefit was partially offset by lower than anticipated volumes, including unplanned curtailments at a couple of our legacy connected fields, the continuing challenges from two of the initial wells at Shenandoah, and a planned turnaround at Salamanca that was moved forward from the fourth quarter into the third quarter.
We expect two new wells from the Monument field to be completed and flow across the Shenandoah facility and on to shore through our oil pipelines by the end of the first quarter of next year.
We expect that rig to next drill and complete a fifth producing well at the Shenandoah field by the end of 2027.

As we see it then, it is not a matter of if, it is really only a matter of when the upstream industry will be able to develop the known and to-be-discovered oil in place throughout the areas served by our critical and irreplaceable pipeline franchise.
Whenever such drilling does occur, we will benefit from it, just as we continue to benefit from the producer activity undertaken over the last three decades.

As a result of these items, in addition to the now lower anticipated volumes discussed above, we will likely be near, or possibly even below, the low end of our original guidance for Adjusted EBITDA for the year.

Having said that, we would reiterate that coming in at the low end of 2026 guidance, or missing the fourth quarter, has little to do with the underlying fundamentals and the ultimate cash flow generating capabilities of our businesses, especially in our largest segment.
Stepping back and keeping everything in focus, 2026 has indeed turned out to be a transformational year for Genesis, just as we anticipated.

We finance maintenance capital expenditures and smaller internal growth projects and distributions primarily with cash generated by our operations.

We have historically funded material growth capital projects (including acquisitions and internal growth projects) with borrowings under our senior secured credit facility, equity issuances (common and preferred units), the issuance of senior unsecured or secured notes, and/or the creation of strategic arrangements to share capital costs through joint ventures or strategic alliances.
